Kevin Patrick Yeary

Republican candidate for Court of Criminal Appeals, Place 4, Texas

Judge, Texas Court of Criminal Appeals, Place 4 (incumbent)

Kevin Patrick Yeary is a Republican who has been the judge in Place 4 on the Texas Court of Criminal Appeals since January 1, 2015, and is seeking a third six-year term. He won the seat in 2014, was re-elected in 2020, and was the Republican nominee from the March 3, 2026 primary. In the November 3, 2026 general election he faces Democrat Audra Riley.

Where Yeary stands

Judicial philosophy
Says politics plays no role in his decisions. Says he applies the law as written and believes in judicial restraint.
Precedent and dissents
Says he follows seven principles of judicial restraint, including that court opinions are not the law itself. Says he often dissents alone when he believes the majority read the law wrong.
State v. Stephens (attorney general's power to prosecute election cases)
Dissented alone in State v. Stephens, arguing that the majority misread the Texas Constitution. Says he faced no political pressure before the ruling.
Crystal Mason illegal-voting case
Was one of four judges who dissented from the majority opinion that upheld the dismissal of Crystal Mason's illegal-voting conviction.

Background

  • Judge, Texas Court of Criminal Appeals, Place 4 (2015–present; elected 2014, re-elected 2020)
  • Former appellate prosecutor in the Bexar, Harris and Dallas County district attorney's offices
  • Former defense attorney in private practice
  • Former briefing attorney (law clerk) at the Texas Court of Criminal Appeals
